What the SDKs do that the spec does not allow

ouo against Sentry, per feature

Step 4's Must and Should features. "Ours" comes from the audits above; "Sentry" from Step 4's vendor research (sentry-javascript 11.11.0, sentry-cocoa 9.33.0, sentry-java 8.63.0, sentry-react-native 8.34.0). Gap: large = Sentry has it, we do not; medium = one level apart; none = level with Sentry; ahead = we have more; target only = neither has it fully, so the gap is to our own target. Effort is a rough size to close it: S up to a week, M one to three weeks, L more.

Overhead

Every number is measured here, on 2026-11-10, on one Apple M5 Mac (10 cores, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1), with ouo and Sentry on the same app and journey per platform and a no-SDK baseline in every round. Web: headless Chromium 156 through Playwright 1.64.1, @ouo11y/browser 0.3.1 against @sentry/browser 11.11.0, 5 rounds (3 at 4x CPU throttling), host load about 2. iOS: Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0), ouo11y-ios 0.3.0 against sentry-cocoa 9.33.0, 12 cold launches and 3 journey rounds, host load about 2 to 3. Android: emulator (API 35, arm64), the Kotlin of sdk/android against sentry-android 8.63.0, 3 rounds, host load about 3 to 5. React Native: JS bundle size only. Simulator and emulator numbers are not device numbers. Medians; whiskers show the lowest and highest run.

ouoSentryNo SDK (baseline)Whiskers: lowest to highest run

Web bundle

Each variant bundled the way an app bundler would (esbuild, minified, ESM, code splitting). "Initial" is what the page downloads at load; ouo loads rrweb lazily, so its replay cost is a second chunk fetched only when replay is sampled. Sentry was bundled with its replay in the main chunk, its default.

Web runtime, 60 s journey, headless Chromium

Chromium 156.0.8078.4, no CPU throttling, 5 interleaved rounds per variant. Values are the SDK's added cost: the variant's median minus the no-SDK median. Whiskers are the lowest and highest run, also minus the no-SDK median.

Web runtime with 4x CPU throttling

The same journey with Chrome's CPU throttled 4x, a rough stand-in for a mid-range phone; 3 rounds.

iOS Simulator

iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0: simulator numbers, not device numbers. One UIKit app built three ways (no SDK, ouo11y-ios 0.3.0, sentry-cocoa 9.33.0); replay is a runtime switch. Size is the arm64 device build. Init: 12 cold launches. CPU, memory and bytes: 3 interleaved rounds of 20 s idle plus a 60 s timer-driven journey, host load about 2 to 3, recorded per run. Values are added over the no-SDK app. Details: measure/ios/README.md.

Android emulator

Android emulator, API 35, arm64, 4 vCPU, software graphics. One native Kotlin app built per variant with R8. ouo here is the Kotlin code the React Native SDK vendors (signals and replay): it has no native exporter, so it sends replay only, while Sentry also sends errors, spans and sessions. CPU counts only the SDKs' own threads plus the main thread's increase, because emulated graphics swamp total CPU. Details: measure/android/README.md.

Not measured

  • Web on Firefox and WebKit: The harness ran Chromium only; the CDP metrics it reads do not exist elsewhere
  • React Native runtime cost: Measuring it needs a release build of the Expo example app on a simulator and emulator, which did not fit this step. The JS bundle and the native pieces (iOS and Android harnesses) were measured separately
  • Real devices: No phone was used. Simulator CPU and memory are the Mac's; the emulator renders in software
  • Web resource timing pricing (SIG-17): The SDK emits no browser.resource_timing events today; initial resources go out as resourceFetch child spans of documentLoad, always on, and are inside the measured telemetry bytes. Step 12 should price the event once it exists
  • Journey spread at n>=5: 3 journey rounds per variant (each round takes about 10 minutes on the simulator); medians with min and max over 3 runs
  • App Store thinned / compressed download size: no signing identity or App Store Connect; reported the unsigned device-arch (arm64) .app plus an IPA-shaped zip instead
  • Device (iPhone) numbers: simulator only by instruction: CPU and memory are the Mac's host process, network is loopback
  • Tap/interaction capture cost: the journey is timer-driven inside the app (no synthesised touches), so neither SDK's tap tracking ran
  • Init time for base: no SDK call to time (baseline)
  • Work done for the app by other processes (backboardd, render server, simulator networking): proc_pid_rusage counts the app process only
  • ouo Android handled-error capture, HTTP spans, traces/logs/metrics export (OTLP) in the native host: sdk/android has no native init, exporter or handled-error/HTTP API today; in the React Native SDK those live in JS (@ouo11y/react-native) and only replay + signals are native. The ouo variants therefore send replay chunks only; the handled error and the 3 HTTP calls per Fetch produce no ouo telemetry, while Sentry reports them (error event, OkHttp spans, transactions, sessions). Wire and CPU deltas are not like-for-like on that part.
  • ouo signals' wire cost (crash / hang / termination reports): Signals writes crash.json/run.json and hands the previous run's report to the host at the next launch; the native host has no sender (the RN JS SDK sends it). No crash or hang was provoked in the journey.
  • ouo full SDK as shipped (React Native app examples/ouo-mobile: JS SDK + native replay + signals): Not run: an RN app's own baseline (Hermes, RN runtime) would swamp a native comparison against sentry-android, and building the Expo example (prebuild + C++ build) was out of the time budget of this step. The native host measures exactly the Kotlin code the RN SDK vendors.
  • Runtime cost of sentry-android with NDK (variant sentryfull): Measured for size only; the NDK handler adds a native crash handler, not per-minute work, and the runtime runs cover sentry-android-core (+replay).
  • Device (real hardware) CPU, memory and energy: Emulator only (no physical phone by rule). Guest GL is emulated (-gpu swiftshader_indirect), so the app's RenderThread burns ~13 s CPU per journey minute even in the baseline; PixelCopy and JPEG/MP4 encoding costs differ from a phone's GPU and hardware codecs (Sentry replay encodes MP4 through MediaCodec, here a software encoder). Battery/energy cannot be measured on an emulator.
  • Frame timing (jank) impact via dumpsys gfxinfo, and simpleperf profiles: Not collected: with emulated GL the frame times reflect the emulator, not the SDKs; per-thread /proc CPU attribution is used instead.
